newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia calls for fair sale of Tyumen Oil Company.
newsitem.headline: Russia calls for fair sale of Tyumen Oil Company.

text.p: Russia will amend the terms of a forthcoming tender of the Tyumen Oil Company, or TNK, after some officials said the sale could favour certain bidders, energy officials said on Thursday.
The change could mean greater competition between the two companies said to be competing for the stake, financial firm the Alfa Group and Rosneftinvest, an unknown.
Fuel and Energy Ministry spokesman Sergei Slesaryev said the ministry had studied the terms of the investment tender for a 40 percent stake and agreed changes were needed.

"There is the possibility of eliminating the inequality (of conditions for bidders) without substantial changes to the terms of the investment tender and, consequently, without moving the sale or privatisation dates forward," he said.

Interfax news agency quoted First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko as saying First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, who is also fuel and energy minister, had ordered the sale not to privilege any one bidder.
The head of TNK oil production unit Nizhnevartovskneftegaz had said last week the terms favoured the Alfa Group.
The quarrel over fair terms revolves around how bids should account for the value of certain TNK equipment and assets.
Under the tender's original terms, a bidder had either to deposit either $88 million in cash, the "value" of the items, or present proof that it owned the items.
Under the new terms, Slesaryev said, only cash would be accepted.

Nizhnevartovskneftegaz director Victor Pali, who has opposed the 40 percent sale, had said Alfa Group units had stakes in the equipment and assets, giving them an edge. Alfa Group could not be reached for comment.
The sale of TNK, one of the last large oil companies to be privatised, is not open to foreign investors.

The tender for the 40 percent stake, set for July 16, carries a price tag of about $25 million for the stock and $160 million in investment over two years. In a separate sale, Russia will offer around 47 percent of TNK through special cash auctions starting August 5.
